# Better Experience
English | 简体中文
A DeepSeek Harness plugin that rewrites the prompt you are about to send — Standard or Professional,
with scene-aware routing — and keeps your account balance and time-of-use pricing in view at the si
-aware routing — and keeps your account balance and time-of-use pricing in view at the sidebar foot.
> **Community plugin.** Independently maintained; not built, reviewed, or supported by DeepSeek. A p
lugin runs with the host's own permissions, so read the source before installing it into a profile t
hat holds real data.

| Package | `@unknowssq/better-experience` — MIT; the first npm release is pending |
| Surface | Web

client (`dsh.client.platform: "web"`): the `web` profile and the Desktop app |

e@link:<path to this checkout>"` |

this checkout>"` |
| Exposes | one host command `/be-optimize`, two HTTP routes, five client slots |
In the package: `index.js` holds the Config schema and the command; `client.js` holds all five slot
contributions as a single `window.__ModuleLoader__` bundle. Verified on dsh `0.2.1-rc.5` (Windows),
last checked 2026-10-31.
## Features
**Prompt optimization**
- **One-click rewrite** — the sparkle button left of Send (`conversation.input.activity`) rewrites t
he current draft in place: only the clean prompt reaches your editor, and nothing else is appended t

o it.
- **Manual only** — nothing rewrites the draft in the background and nothing delays a send. Th
e draft changes only when you press the button; Enter always submits exactly what is in the composer

.
- **Two fixed modes** — Standard keeps the rewrite concise while clarifying the request; Professio

nal models task complexity and adds execution and acceptance detail when needed.
- **Scene routing**
— `professional` either classifies the scene itself (`auto`) or is pinned to one of eight scenes (`
coding`, `writing`, `research`, `data`, `creative`, `business`, `agent`, `general`). `coding` additi

onally enables the implementation sub-scene rules.
- **Output language** — follow the draft's langua
ge, or pin Chinese / English.
**Undo without leaving the composer**
- **The button becomes undo** — right after a rewrite the same button switches to an undo icon. One

click puts the pre-optimization draft back verbatim, and the sparkle returns.
- **A hand edit retire
s the slot** — as soon as you change the draft yourself, the undo state is dropped, so the button ca

n never restore text over edits it did not make.
- **Typing keys stay the host's** — the plugin regi
sters no `Ctrl+Z` / `Ctrl+Y` binding. Undo and redo inside the composer keep the host editor's own b
`Ctrl+Z` / `Ctrl+Y` binding. Undo and redo inside the composer keep the host editor's own behaviour.
**Awareness while you write**
- **Balance and price card** — mounted at `sidebar.footer.action`: current balance, a peak / off-pea
k chip counting down to the next switch, and the cache-hit input price for Flash and V4 Pro at that
period. It polls every 60 s, refreshes on focus or tab return, keeps the last snapshot as *stale* in

stead of flashing an error, and collapses to a wallet icon with a status dot in the rail.
[该节后续省略]
## Requirements
| Requirement | Detail |

| dsh | `>=0.2.1-rc.5` (`engines.dsh` in `package.json`) |
| Client bundle | The Web client (`@deeps

eek-ai/dsh-web-app`). A host-only profile loads the plugin but has no UI. |
| Default model | `/be-o
ptimize` calls the currently selected model through `ctx.llm`; with no selection it answers 「没有可用模型，

请先配置模型」. |
| Optional services | `fs` and `webServer`. Both are probed, not injected — without them

the template route is simply not registered. |
| Node / pnpm | Whatever the DSH runtime ships. The p
lugin itself has one runtime dependency, `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`. |
## Installation
The package is named `@unknowssq/better-experience` and is prepared for npm, but `0.1.0` is not on t
he registry yet, so the verified install today is a linked checkout. Both forms are covered below: o
nce `0.1.0` is published, `add` takes the bare package name and the checkout is only needed when you
blished, `add` takes the bare package name and the checkout is only needed when you edit the source.
## Architecture
`client.js` is one bundle: dsh loads third-party clients through `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id,
factory(require) })`, where `require()` resolves the host module registry rather than the filesyste
m. Modularity therefore comes from in-file sections — Constants → Locale → Pure Logic → Hooks → UI C
omponents → Styles → `apply` — with a one-way dependency rule and named CSS constants instead of sep
Styles → `apply` — with a one-way dependency rule and named CSS constants instead of separate files.
Full partition, dependency rules, and style lifecycle: `docs/plugin-architecture.md`, kept with the
development checkout rather than inside the published package.
Design constraints worth knowing before editing:
- **Tokens only.** Every colour comes from host design tokens (`--dsw-alias-*`, `--dsw-radius-*`, `-
-dsw-shadow-*`); no host selector is restyled, and no colour is hardcoded. One `<style>` element is

created in `apply` and removed by its cleanup function.
- **Left-aligned panel.** `.be-settings` use

s `margin:0` with `max-width:560px`, so heading, cards, and rows share one left edge.
- **Auto-width
footer card.** `.be-foot-card` is `width:fit-content` capped by `max-width:calc(100% - 8px)`; the l
eft column is `flex:0 1 auto; min-width:0` so only the balance ellipsizes, while the price column ne
s `flex:0 1 auto; min-width:0` so only the balance ellipsizes, while the price column never shrinks.
## Compatibility

| Verified | dsh `0.2.1-rc.5`, Windows, 2026-10-31 (web profile and Desktop app) |
| Minimum | `engi

nes.dsh` `>=0.2.1-rc.5` |
| Not verified | Headless / SDK / ACP profiles — the plugin's value is its
UI, and the client half does not load there. Host logic is independent of the UI but has not been e

xercised in those profiles. |
| Breaking changes | This is a `0.x`-era plugin tracking a `0.2.1-rc.x
` host; slot names, the command envelope, and the template route are the parts most likely to move.
host; slot names, the command envelope, and the template route are the parts most likely to move. |
